comparator.name: Arts and Culture Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target names the Dutch-taught Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen specialisation, so that exact formal route is reconstructed rather than the English Arts and Culture Studies or Society, Language and Culture routes. The 2026-2027 programme-specific OER establishes a coherent 180-EC pathway: a fixed 60-EC first year, 30 EC of fixed second-year ACW study plus two 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors, and a third year with 20 EC of fixed or restricted-choice ACW study, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine free space. For the formal one-of-two 5-EC third-year choice, Het Veranderende Landschap is selected by the neutral curriculum-order tie-break. The later prospective year pages are used only for current programme descriptions and corroboration; the applicable 2026-2027 OER controls the formal component list and weights.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target itself names Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen. The 2026-2027 OER distinguishes it from the Arts and Culture Studies and Society, Language and Culture specialisations, so the exact Dutch ACW route is reconstructed.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad cross-arts, visual-art, theory, historical and international interests. Two further generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible at UCR: culture, identity and power; and literature, film and cultural communication. The pairwise differences are seven to fourteen courses, and each route has a distinct academic organisation. A further performance, music and cultural-production direction remains evidenced, but the maximum of three alternatives has been reached; UCR also lacks a dedicated music or performing-arts sequence.

alternatives.label: Arts, media & cultural analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates art history and heritage, literature, film and media, philosophy, sociology, history, communication and qualitative and historical research.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines visual art and heritage, literature, film and media with cultural theory, history, sociology, ethics, criticism, creative communication and qualitative, historical and art-historical research.
progression: Introductory art history, literary studies, film and media, history and sociology precede advanced museum studies, media and race, film and text, social theory, cultural communication and independent research. The schedule observes the available semesters and develops foundational interpretive work before advanced research and criticism.

alternatives.label: Culture, identity & power
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum studies culture through history, political thought, sociology, media, literature, heritage, social movements and international and European politics, with sustained attention to identity and power.
alternatives.concept: A social and political cultural-studies route organised around identity, ideology and power across history, media, literature, art and heritage, supported by sociology, political philosophy, comparative and international politics, social movements and qualitative and historical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces most art-history, film, literary-analysis and creative-communication study with political philosophy, comparative and international politics, empire, gender history, social movements, heritage and conflict. Fourteen of the 24 courses differ, and culture is organised around identity and power rather than broad analysis across artistic media.
progression: Foundations in history, political philosophy, sociology, gender, ethics, comparative politics, media and literature precede advanced social theory, EU politics, media and race, heritage, conflict and historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Literature, film & cultural communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum forms a clear sequence in literature, film, media, rhetoric and creative communication, complemented by art history, archaeology, philosophy, history and qualitative research.
alternatives.concept: A text, screen and communication route connecting literary interpretation, film and media analysis, adaptation, documentary, rhetoric and creative communication with art history, world archaeology, philosophy and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes broad art-history coverage, Renaissance study, sociology, social theory and historical research. It adds rhetoric, world archaeology, environmental media, philosophy and advanced persuasive communication, with seven courses differing from the closest match and fourteen from the identity-and-power route. The organising emphasis is interpretation and communication across text and screen.
progression: Introductions to literature, media and rhetoric precede advanced film-and-text, media-and-race, literary-meaning, persuasive-communication and creative-communication work. Historical, archaeological, philosophical and qualitative foundations support comparative interpretation. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

Both require sustained independent research, source analysis and a substantial written argument; UCR's seminar is course-based rather than a separate thesis.

notes.text: Both programmes study art and culture through history, theory, interpretation, media and research. The Radboud programme additionally requires dedicated analysis of music and includes specialist study of opera, musical theatre and performance culture, alongside two Faculty of Arts minors, professional festival work and substantial free-choice space. UCR offers strong combinations in art history, literature, film and media, communication, history, philosophy, sociology and politics, but no dedicated music-analysis or performing-arts sequence.
